1. Let \(G\) represent a gray square and \(W\) a white square. The original board is

\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
G&G&G&W&W\\
G&G&W&G&G\\
G&G&G&G&G\\
W&G&G&G&G\\
W&W&G&G&G
\end{array}
\]

2. A \(270^\circ\) clockwise turn is equivalent to a \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise turn.

3. Under this rotation, the original rightmost column becomes the top row, and each successive column becomes the next row:

\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
W&G&G&G&G\\
W&G&G&G&G\\
G&W&G&G&G\\
G&G&G&G&W\\
G&G&G&W&W
\end{array}
\]

This matches Board A. The colored edges confirm this: the green left edge moves to the bottom, while the orange bottom edge moves to the right.
